title: Swapping Pieces: Replace the Queen’s Defense
summary: Use a rook sacrifice and a knight reroute to force the defender on g8 to become a rook, enabling smothered mate.

nodes.question: How can White replace the defender of g8?
nodes.explanation: Re8+ forces the rook from e1 onto e8. Then Nf7+/Nh6+ repositions the knight to protect g8, and Qg8+ can force the rook onto that square before Nf7 mate.

branches.title: Source finish: rook replacement and smothered mate
commentary: Begin after ...Kh8. White’s knight on d8 blocks the black queen on b8 from reaching e8 along the back rank.
Re8+ offers the remaining white rook on the back rank. The black queen cannot pass through the knight on d8 to capture it or interpose farther along the rank.
Rxe8 is the sole legal reply. The rook from e1 takes the sacrifice and becomes the defender White wants to divert to g8.
Nf7+ checks h8 and prepares the knight’s route to h6. It is important to reposition before offering the queen.
Kg8 is the sole legal reply. The king leaves the corner while the rook remains on e8.
Nh6+ gives double check: the knight attacks g8 and vacates the a2–g8 diagonal for Qa2. Only king moves can answer both checks; Kh8 and Kf8 are legal.
Kh8 chooses the source corner retreat. Black’s g7 and h7 pawns leave little room around the king.
Qg8+ offers the queen beside the king. Nh6 protects g8, so Kxg8 is illegal. Qb8 cannot reach g8 because its own rook on e8 blocks the rank.
Rxg8 is the sole legal reply. The rook takes the queen and now occupies g8, blocking its own king’s escape.
Nf7# checks h8. Black’s own Rg8, g7 pawn and h7 pawn fill the king’s three adjacent squares; a knight check cannot be blocked.
branches.explanation: Nf7# checks h8. Black’s own Rg8, g7 pawn and h7 pawn fill the king’s three adjacent squares; a knight check cannot be blocked.

branches.title: Independent defense: retreat to f8 instead
commentary: Check the other king retreat after the double check rather than assuming Black must return to h8.
Re8+ forces the rook onto the back rank.
Rxe8 is the only legal answer and replaces the distant rook with a nearby defender.
Nf7+ checks the corner king and begins the reroute.
Kg8 is forced because the knight check leaves no other legal king move.
Nh6+ gives double check from the knight and queen. Kf8 is a legal alternative to the illustrated Kh8.
Kf8 declines the corner, but puts the king next to the protected mating square f7.
Qf7# checks f8. Nh6 protects f7, Qf7 covers e7/g7 and g8, and Black’s rook on e8 occupies the remaining back-rank flight.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qf7# checks f8. Nh6 protects f7, Qf7 covers e7/g7 and g8, and Black’s rook on e8 occupies the remaining back-rank flight.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t White offer Qg8 immediately after Rxe8?
exercises.answer: With the knight still on d8, g8 is unprotected and Kxg8 is legal. The Nf7/Nh6 reroute is essential.

exercises.prompt: Does Nh6+ force the king back to h8?
exercises.answer: No. Kf8 is also legal, but Qf7 mates. Kh8 instead permits the queen sacrifice and smothered mate.

sourceCorrections.claim: After the double check the king has to return to the corner.
